summary.headline: AJAX FY26 revenue rose to INR2,103 crore (from INR2,074 crore) while EBITDA margin fell to 12.6%; Q4 EBITDA margin recovered to 15.1% after a 2% price hike.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue was about INR2,103 crore against INR2,074 crore in FY25, with SLCM revenue flat at INR1,758 crore on a 4% volume decline. EBITDA fell to INR266 crore (12.6% margin) from INR318 crore (15.3%), reflecting CEV5 production costs, lower operating leverage and calibrated pricing. Q4 FY26 was the turnaround quarter: revenue was flat YoY at INR758 crore, gross margin rose 170 bps to 25.8%, and EBITDA grew about 4% to INR115 crore with a 15.1% margin, helped by a 2% January price increase and direct material cost reductions. Management said it has regained market share to 73.5% in FY26 from about 69.8% in Q1, and that competitors have not taken price increases. Management gave no FY27 volume or margin guidance beyond an intent to reach early double-digit growth and 13-15% margins over the medium term.

segments.name: SLCM
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,758 crore, flat YoY on about 4% volume decline vs industry about 11%; market share 73.5% for FY26 (about 69.8% low in Q1). Q4 SLCM volumes down about 7% YoY with revenue flat on price and mix.

segments.name: Non-SLCM (pumps, batching plants)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 7% in FY26 on volume growth. Management cites 4-series and 7-series pumps and 38m and 44m boom pumps, and higher-capacity batching plants as picking up.

segments.name: Spares and service
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 9% in FY26 despite lower average machine running hours, supported by dealer and service network expansion.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue has grown to about INR103 crore from about INR74 crore; one slipform paver sold to Saudi Arabia in March with revenue expected in Q4. Management guides 20-25% export growth for FY27.

segments.name: Udaan (SLCM sub-line)
segments.commentary: FY26 Udaan volumes about 202 units. Management says Udaan sits within SLCM and it aims for 2-3x that volume in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance. Management's stated intent is early double-digit growth (mid-to-early double digits), not 15%, with FY27 H1 weaker and H2 stronger (about 40:60 split).
Medium-term aim to return to mid-teens growth and 13-15% EBITDA margin; management says FY27 achievement depends on demand, steel prices and pricing.
Working capital guidance of about 30 days as a normalised level (25-30 days as aggressive range).
Export growth of 20-25% expected for FY27.
Udaan volume target of 2-3x FY26 levels (about 202 units) if conditions allow.
Management expects some Maharashtra turnaround in H2 FY27, a possible Gujarat and Rajasthan contribution, and a weaker outlook for Madhya Pradesh.
Capital deployment: an opportunity to be examined with a decision expected in H2 FY27; the company says it will not pursue turnarounds, weak governance or sunset sectors.
capex_capacity: Dealer inventory about 35-40 days in most locations, with some markets 4-5 days higher on slowing demand.
Active machine population about 35,000-38,000 units; trade-in programme being built on a database of customers aged 5-8 years.
Product scope: AJAX claims to be the only Indian player doing slipform pavers and 3D printing at scale; it is an asset-light model.
Management says it has no concrete acquisition target on the table.
demand_pricing: Central capex FY26 budget INR11.21 lakh crore, revised to INR10.96 lakh crore; utilisation about 55% until December 2025. State payment delays in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh constrain customer cash flow.
Price increase of 2% taken in Q4 (January), applied across the ARGO portfolio; management says peers have not taken any increase.
Management cites a 5-6% average price gap vs competitors (range 4-10%), after CEV5 transition.
Market share 73.5% in FY26; about 76% in April 2026; Oct-Dec quarter about 76-78%. Management says share held through Feb and March.
Input cost pressure from steel, fuel and cement; geopolitics, El Nino and interest rates flagged as risks.

Gujarat is strong on agrarian-to-commercial land conversion and the Commonwealth Games infrastructure; Uttar Pradesh is expected to see spending ahead of elections; Andhra Pradesh is doing well; Madhya Pradesh has no green shoots yet.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 demand outlook: can volume growth reach 15%, Udaan volumes, and state-level recovery (Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to 15%; it expects mid-to-early double-digit growth with a stronger H2. Maharashtra may turn around in H2, MP shows no green shoots, and Gujarat, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan are expected to grow.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital outlook for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: A normalised 30 days is a good number for the year, with 25-30 days as an aggressive range. The key watch item is government cash flow reaching contractors and dealers.

qa_highlights.question: Will SLCM realisations rise another 1-2% on the higher base?
qa_highlights.answer: The company took a 2% price increase in Q4 and intends to recover further cost increases from the market where possible; steel and fuel costs remain pressures. No further figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 given commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: The medium-term aim is 13-15% margin. Management said it is hard to predict FY27 and that holding current margins is a good outcome until volumes recover.

qa_highlights.question: Udaan volumes and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 volume was about 202 units, and management would be delighted with 2-3x that in FY27. Udaan revenue sits within SLCM.

qa_highlights.question: Cash deployment and inorganic options?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not do turnarounds, invest where governance is weak, or enter sunset sectors. No acquisition is on the table; a decision may come in H2 and is aimed at growth through M&A or assets with quick market traction.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that competitors dump inventory at lower prices and force AJAX to reverse its price hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says competitors have had the same period to act and that the 5-6% price gap has not hurt demand. It would respond with calibrated action rather than cutting prices.

risks_watch: Government capex execution gap (about 55% utilisation to December 2025) and state payment delays in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh.
Price hike sustainability: competitors have taken no increases; a 5-6% price gap could bring share loss if rivals discount.
Steel, fuel and cement cost inflation and possible geopolitical effects on export markets (Africa, Middle East).
Working capital back-up if receivables stretch; dealer stock in some markets 4-5 days above norm.
Capital allocation: about INR1,121 crore cash with an M&A decision expected in H2 FY27; dividend policy is for the board.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the company's franchise, pricing and cash generation, but cautious and non-committal on FY27 volumes, demand timing and margin recovery. The CEO repeatedly declined to give numerical guidance, citing uncertainty, and gave generic answers on fuel economics and competitor pricing.
key_quotes: Our SLCM volume degrowth for the year remained limited to about 4% compared to an estimated construction equipment industry decline at about 11%.
I am not giving a guidance that in FY '27 this would happen.

I anticipate at this point in time a mid and early double-digit growth would be a good number to look at and as we progress forward, I think we would be in a better position to see how things progress.
I can say this with conviction as we speak none of our competitors have taken a rupee of price increase.

growth.why: Management's intent is mid-to-early double-digit FY27 volume growth (about 10% midpoint), with no formal guidance and no specific capacity, orders or contracts behind it; backing rests on demand recovery, share gains and pricing, and Q4 FY26 revenue was flat YoY at INR758 crore.
